What to do & what you should see: Drag ACTIVITY UNIT from the left palette onto the canvas. A dialog titled 'Activity Unit Form' opens with two sections (Gene Product, Function Description); Save is greyed out.
Fill Molecular Function (type, click a suggestion) and Gene Product. Save turns active. Click Save; a new activity appears on the canvas. (No evidence needed for just these two.)

Test: TC 1.3 Required field empty blocks Save
What to do & what you should see: Fill only Molecular Function and leave Gene Product empty. Save stays greyed out; the 'Why is the Save button disabled?' link explains the missing required item. Fill Gene Product; Save activates.

On the Molecular Function row use the three-dots menu > Add Context > 'part of' (Biological Process) and 'occurs in' (Cellular Component). New rows appear; fill each term. Each new row shows empty Reference/With columns.

Test: TC 1.5 Filled context row needs evidence
What to do & what you should see: With a Biological Process term filled but no evidence, Save is greyed out and the 'Why disabled?' popup says it 'requires at least one evidence'. Add evidence (code + PMID:12345); Save activates and saves.
On a context row with an evidence code, type '12345' (no prefix) - Save stays disabled. 'FOO:123' also rejected. 'PMID:12345' (or DOI:/GO_REF:) makes Save active.

Test: TC 1.7 Evidence code with no reference blocks Save
What to do & what you should see: Fill an evidence code but leave Reference empty - Save disabled; popup says you provided an evidence but no reference. Add PMID:12345; Save activates.
Click Clear; the form resets to empty. Close the dialog; anything not saved is not on the canvas.
Drag CHEMICAL onto the canvas. Dialog titled 'Chemical Form' opens. First section is 'Chemical', second is 'Location (optional)'. The chemical row has no Reference/With columns.

Test: TC 2.2 Chemical search returns chemicals only
What to do & what you should see: In the Chemical box type a chemical (e.g. glucose, ATP) - only chemical (ChEBI) suggestions appear. A gene name like BRCA1 does NOT appear.

Test: TC 2.3 Chemical row hides inapplicable menu items
What to do & what you should see: Open the chemical row's three-dots menu. It does NOT offer Search Annotations, Fill with root term, or ISS/ISO/IC. It does still offer Add Context.
Add Context > 'located in' (Cellular Component); a Location row appears. Removing it or leaving Location empty still allows Save (Location is optional).
With just the Chemical term filled, Save is active. Click Save; a chemical node (a circle) appears on the canvas.
Drag PROTEIN COMPLEX onto the canvas. Dialog titled 'Protein Complex Form' opens. An amber note warns it should be used rarely. The Molecular Function row is visible and editable.

Test: TC 3.2 Complex term accepts GO complex terms
What to do & what you should see: Fill Molecular Function. In the Protein Complex row (Gene Product section) type a complex name (e.g. proteasome) - GO complex term suggestions appear; pick one.
The Protein Complex row's menu is a + (plus) button offering 'has part' > Gene Product. Add two gene-product subunits and fill their terms. Each subunit has a remove option.

Test: TC 3.4 No complex inside a complex
What to do & what you should see: On a gene-product subunit row, Add Context must NOT offer 'part of > Protein Complex'.

Test: TC 3.5 Add function context and save
What to do & what you should see: On the Molecular Function row add 'part of' (BP) and/or 'occurs in' (CC) with a term and one evidence (PMID:12345). Save activates; the complex appears on the canvas listing its subunits.
On a context row use three-dots > Evidence > Add evidence. An empty evidence appears with evidence code, Reference, and With boxes. Add a second the same way.
Click the evidence code box, type a few letters (e.g. direct assay); a dropdown of evidence codes appears; click one to fill it.

Test: TC 4.3 Reference must be DB:accession (allowed DBs only)
What to do & what you should see: Click the Reference box - an editor opens with a database dropdown (PMID/DOI/GO_REF) and an accession field. PMID + a real id may show an article preview. A bare number or a made-up prefix like FOO:1 is not accepted.
Click the With box - choose a database and accession (e.g. UniProtKB + id). A value must contain a colon or Save is blocked. Leaving With empty is fine.
three-dots > Evidence > ISS auto-fills code ECO:0000250 + GO_REF:0000024. ISO = ECO:0000266 + GO_REF:0000024. IC = ECO:0000305 + GO_REF:0000036.
On a row with evidence, Evidence > Remove Evidence (or the trash icon) removes the evidence.

Test: TC 4.8 Evidence row menu (editing existing activity)
What to do & what you should see: In the Add Evidence dialog (from the right-side table), each evidence row has its own three-dots menu: Add evidence, ISS, ISO, IC, Clear Values, Delete. Clear Values empties the row; Delete is disabled when only one row remains; ISS/ISO/IC replace the current row.

Test: TC 4.9 See which databases are allowed
What to do & what you should see: Click the info (i) icons next to the Reference and With column headers. Reference popover lists PMID/DOI/GO_REF; With popover lists a longer set of allowed databases.
Type a reference with a leading/trailing space; note whether it is cleaned up or rejected (area still being worked on).
In a term box type 2-3 letters; after a short pause a dropdown of terms (name + id) appears. Click one to fill the box. Typing without clicking does NOT select a term.
A single character shows no dropdown. After getting results, deleting back to empty hides the suggestions.

Test: TC 5.3 Already-used terms appear before typing
What to do & what you should see: In a model with existing activities, click into a term box without typing - a short list of terms already used in the model is offered.

Test: TC 5.4 Each box offers only the right kind of term
What to do & what you should see: Molecular Function box = MF terms only; Location/CC box = CC terms only (no protein complexes); Chemical box = chemicals only (no gene products); Protein Complex box = GO complex terms; Evidence code box = evidence codes.
In a Reference editor choose PMID; typing an accession may show suggestions and/or an article title preview. Switching to DOI/GO_REF changes what is accepted.
Type a nonsense string (e.g. zzzqqq) - the dropdown shows no matches (empty/no-results), not an error.
If a gene has a 'canonical' entry, note whether it appears at/near the top of suggestions (area still being worked on).

Test: TC 6.1 Needs a gene product first
What to do & what you should see: In a new Activity Unit with no gene product, three-dots > Search Annotations shows a message to add a gene product first. After filling a gene product, it opens.

Test: TC 6.2 Pick a term and its evidence
What to do & what you should see: With a gene product set, open Search Annotations on a function/process/component row. Select a term; an evidence table appears. Tick evidences. Done is disabled until a term is selected. Click Done; the row fills with the term AND all ticked evidences.
Type something in the form first. Open Search Annotations then Cancel (or Escape, or click outside). The form still shows everything you typed - nothing lost.

Test: TC 6.4 Picker stacks on top of the form
What to do & what you should see: With Search Annotations open the form stays visible underneath. Escape or background click closes only the picker, not the form.
Hover an activity edge until a connection point appears; drag to a second activity and release on it. A connector form opens naming the source and target.

Choose a relationship (e.g. Regulation, Provides input for, Removes input for, Constitutively upstream, Undetermined). For a regulation an Effect direction (Positive/Negative) and a Directness (Direct/Indirect) appear. A 'suggested causal relation' label updates as you choose.

Test: TC 7.3 Save blocked until valid relation
What to do & what you should see: Before enough choices are made Save is greyed out and a 'Why disabled?' explanation is available. A complete valid relation makes Save active.
Add an evidence (code + PMID:12345) like on activity rows; you can also save without evidence.
Click Save; a success message 'Causal relation successfully created.' appears; the dialog closes and a labelled arrow appears between the two activities.
Double-click an existing arrow; the connector form re-opens with current values. Change the relationship and Save; the arrow updates.
In the connector form for an existing arrow, click Delete; confirm; the arrow is removed.

Choose 'Provides input for'; a 'Connect via Chemical Intermediate' button appears. It opens a chemical connector listing candidate molecules grouped (both / only first / only second). Save is blocked with none selected; tick one+ and Save.

Test: TC 7.9 Cannot connect an activity to itself
What to do & what you should see: Drag a connection from an activity back onto the same activity - it is not allowed; no connector form opens.

Test: TC 7.10 Cannot draw a duplicate arrow
What to do & what you should see: With one arrow already between A and B, try to draw a second from A to B - it is not created (only one connection allowed between the same pair).
Hover an activity; an edit (pencil) icon appears. Click it (or double-click the node); the form opens titled 'Edit ...'. Change a term or add context and Save; the node updates.

Test: TC 8.2 Edit via the right-side table
What to do & what you should see: Single-click an activity; the right drawer opens on the Activity Table tab. Click a term cell to edit just that field. Use Add Context to add a child, or Add Evidence to open the evidence dialog.

Hover an activity; a duplicate icon appears (between edit and delete). Click it; the form opens prefilled with a copy (title is NOT 'Edit'). Save makes a brand-new activity; the original is unchanged. The original's arrows are NOT copied.
Hover an activity; a delete (trash) icon appears. Click it; a confirmation warns it cannot be undone. Confirm; the node and its arrows disappear. (Cancel instead = nothing deleted.)

Test: TC 8.5 Editing a chemical shows chemical labels
What to do & what you should see: Edit a chemical activity. Header reads 'Chemical' (e.g. Edit Chemical / Chemical Form); sections are 'Chemical' and 'Location (optional)', not generic 'Activity/Function Description'. No evidence column and no 'no evidence present' text.
Click the comment icon in the top toolbar; a Comments dialog opens. With none yet it shows 'No comments yet'.
Click Add Comment; a text box appears. The button becomes 'Add Another Comment'; add a second. Save closes the dialog. The comment icon shows a count badge.
Add a box but leave it empty (or spaces only) and Save; the blank comment is dropped and not counted.

Test: TC 9.4 Removing a written comment confirms
What to do & what you should see: Click the trash icon next to a comment with text; a confirmation 'Remove this comment? This cannot be undone.' appears; confirm to remove. Removing an empty box removes it immediately (no confirmation).
After saving, reopen the dialog (or reload the model); your comments are still there.

Test: TC 10.1 Untitled model can be named
What to do & what you should see: Toolbar shows 'Untitled' (grey italics) when there is no title. Click the pencil next to the title; an Edit Title dialog opens. Save is disabled while empty. Type a title; Save activates; click Save; the toolbar shows your title.
Click the title pencil again, change the text, Save; the toolbar updates. Open again and Cancel; the title is unchanged.

Click the coloured state tag (has a small pencil); a Change State dialog opens with a State dropdown. Pick a different state and Save; the tag updates (colour may change). Open again and Cancel; state unchanged.
Find the date chip (calendar icon) and click it; nothing should happen (it is not a button and must not open a dialog or break).
An activity node shows its gene product and molecular function; a chemical is drawn as a circle; a protein complex shows its subunits.

Test: TC 11.2 Connector arrows show the relation
What to do & what you should see: An arrow shows the relation (e.g. positively regulates). Positive vs negative relations look different (arrowhead shape / colour).
Hover an activity; edit, duplicate, and delete icons appear on its edge. Move the mouse away; the icons hide.
Drag nodes into a messy arrangement; click Auto Layout (top layout bar); the activities rearrange tidily.
Open the Detail menu (Default / Simple View / Preview); switching changes how much detail nodes show.
Open the Spacing menu (Compact View / Expanded View); switching changes the gap between activities.
Use zoom in / out buttons (top-right of the layout bar); the canvas scales. Reset zoom returns to the default scale.
Drag a node to a new spot; its position stays (e.g. after reloading the model the node is where you left it).
For a protein complex, its gene-product subunits (has part links) are visible on the graph and in the right-side table.

Test: TC 12.1 Error chip appears only with errors
What to do & what you should see: If the model has problems a red 'N Errors Found' chip shows near the title; with no problems no chip shows.
Click the 'N Errors Found' chip; the right drawer opens a 'Validation Errors' panel with three count boxes: Data model violation errors (ShEx), Activity Units / Chemicals errors, Relations errors.

Test: TC 12.3 Count matches what is listed
What to do & what you should see: Compare the chip number with the problems actually shown in the panel; note any mismatch (known sore point).

Test: TC 12.4 Each listed error is understandable
What to do & what you should see: Each red ShEx card shows a number and a plain message, plus a small subject>relation>object diagram. Note any message that is confusing or refers to something not in your model.

Test: TC 12.5 Activity and relation problem lists
What to do & what you should see: The Activity Units/Chemicals section may list 'Node not shown' and 'Node/relation combination not allowed' items; the Relations section lists specific edges. Check each matches something really wrong.
Click Close (top-right); the drawer closes; the error chip is still on the toolbar (closing does not clear errors).
